This module cites no ISO text — ISO/IEC 27001's structure (what an ISMS certification actually
certifies, Stage 1/Stage 2 audits, surveillance audits, scope, the Statement of Applicability, and
a few widely known general control-domain categories) is named and described only, the same
handling this curriculum gives every paid, proprietary framework (ISO 31000, ISO 19011, GAMP 5,
and, last module, SOC 2). No specific Annex A control number is asserted anywhere in the lesson.

**A note on ISO's own catalogue page, read before anything else below:** this session tried,
directly, to find and verify ISO's own public listing page for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 — the same page
`reading-a-soc-2-report`'s sibling modules elsewhere in this curriculum (`risk-frameworks-side-by-
side` for ISO 31000, `designing-an-internal-audit-program` for ISO 19011) were able to confirm
through a Wayback Machine snapshot. For ISO 27001, that path didn't work this time: a direct `curl`
against `iso.org` returned HTTP 403 on every page tried, including the site's own root — the same
bot-protection block this curriculum has hit before, just wider this time. The Internet Archive's
Wayback Machine availability API, tried several times across this session with pauses in between,
returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) every time; its CDX API alternative was blocked outright by this
environment's own egress policy. A national-standards-body guess (a specific ANSI webstore URL)
also returned 403. Rather than publish an unverified ISO catalogue number — which this module's own
guardrails explicitly forbid — no direct ISO.org link appears below. In its place are two
independent, directly `curl`-verified pages from accredited certification bodies that describe
ISO/IEC 27001's certification structure in their own words, neither one ISO's own site:

- **[BSI: ISO 27001 — Information Security Management](https://www.bsigroup.com/en-GB/iso-27001-information-security/)**
  — the British Standards Institution's own public page describing ISO/IEC 27001 and its
  certification process (BSI is itself a national standards body and an accredited ISO 27001
  certification body, not ISO's own publishing arm). Curl-verified this session: HTTP 200, page
  title confirmed as "ISO 27001 - Information Security Management | BSI UK." Useful for the general
  shape of the certification process (initial audit stages, surveillance audits) in a certification
  body's own words — not a source of the standard's exact text, which remains a paid publication
  this curriculum has never purchased or quoted.

- **[NQA: ISO 27001 for Information Security](https://www.nqa.com/en-us/certification/standards/iso-27001)**
  — a second, independent accredited certification body's own public overview page, included for
  redundancy since the primary source (ISO's own site) couldn't be verified this session. Curl-
  verified this session: HTTP 200, page title confirmed as "ISO 27001 for Information Security | Get
  Certified." Same caveat as above: describes the certification process in the certifying body's own
  words, not a substitute for the standard's own paid text.

- **[Reading a SOC 2 Report](../reading-a-soc-2-report/index.qmd)** — module 2 of this course, where
  the device-management platform vendor's own SOC 2 report was read for the first time (Type II,
  Security and Availability certain, Confidentiality plausible, the CUEC finding, the bridge-letter
  determination). Read it first if you haven't: this module assumes those findings and treats this
  certificate as a different, complementary kind of assurance about the same vendor, not a restatement
  of the same one.

**If you're verifying these links yourself later:** try ISO's own catalogue page directly before
relying on the two certification-body pages above — this session's block may not be permanent, and
ISO's own page (when reachable) is always the better primary reference for the standard's scope and
purchase information.

**Added on 2026-11-11: verification, accreditation, and Statement of Applicability depth.**

- **[Part 1: ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability (SoA)
  Explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jSVbrqZ6c-Q)** (Pyramid Certifications, from oEmbed
  `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson, from an ISO certification body. General ISO
  27001 training, not blood-specific. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[IAFCertSearch - the global database for accredited
  certifications](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDEaHPawzVA)** (IAF CertSearch, from oEmbed
  `author_name`) — a short official explainer from the International Accreditation Forum's own
  channel on how to confirm that a certificate was issued by an accredited certification body and
  is listed. Watch it before you verify the vendor's certificate. Verified embeddable via YouTube
  oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[IAF CertSearch](https://iafcertsearch.org/)** — the International Accreditation Forum's
  global database of accredited certifications. Use it to look up whether a vendor's certificate is
  actually listed by an accredited certification body, rather than relying on a PDF or a website
  badge. Not every valid certificate is necessarily listed, so a missing entry is a question to ask
  the vendor, not proof of fraud. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[IAF: about the Multilateral Recognition Arrangement](https://iaf.nu/en/about-iaf-mla/)** —
  the International Accreditation Forum's own page on the arrangement under which accreditation
  bodies recognize each other's accredited certificates. Read it to understand why "issued by an
  accredited certification body" is a meaningful thing to check. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[UKAS: United Kingdom Accreditation Service](https://www.ukas.com/)** — an example national
  accreditation body, the kind of organization that accredits certification bodies. Use it to see
  who checks the checkers; a certificate's issuing body should name its accreditation body.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISMS.online: ISO 27001 Statement of
  Applicability](https://www.isms.online/iso-27001/statement-of-applicability/)** — a vendor-written
  (ISMS software company) explainer of what an SoA contains and how exclusions are justified. It is
  a commercial source, so treat it as a plain-language aid and not as the standard. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about vetting a vendor's ISO 27001 certificate.

- **[Reviewing an ISO 27001 certificate: a checklist](https://blog.nviso.eu/2020/06/10/reviewing-an-iso-27001-certificate-a-checklist/)** (NVISO Labs, security consultancy) — a step-by-step reading of what's printed on a certificate: scope, issuing body, dates. Written in 2020, so check any edition details against the current standard. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[How to Verify a Vendor's ISO 27001 Certificate](https://www.thoropass.com/blog/verify-vendor-iso-27001-certificate)** (Thoropass — vendor/commercial content) — practical tips on spotting scope gaps and unaccredited issuers. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Five Key Considerations for Avoiding Complacency in Third Party Security Management and Monitoring](https://www.isaca.org/resources/news-and-trends/newsletters/atisaca/2025/volume-23/five-key-considerations-for-avoiding-complacency-in-third-party-security-management-and-monitoring)** (ISACA @ISACA newsletter, 2025) — a short caution against treating a certification as the end of due diligence. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
